scores.verdict: The colour work, the Cormorant/Manrope pairing, the dark-theme depth and the card rhythm are genuinely lovely, and the palette's contrast maths is better than most production apps I audit. But the type scale is not a design system — it is 130+ ad-hoc font-size declarations below 12px, bottoming out at 3px, plus a live text-corruption bug. No amount of palette craft survives that.

must_fix_to_reach_8.change: Replace the four ad-hoc rules in the "Legibility refinements" block with a real floor. Define --text-xs: 11px; --text-sm: 12px; --text-base: 13px on :root (lines 9-32), then sweep every font-size below 11px to var(--text-xs). There are ~130. Delete rather than raise only the purely decorative cover rules (:1401, :1445, :1453, :2205-2211, :2546-2552, :2671), whose container should get aria-hidden instead.
must_fix_to_reach_8.rationale: The "Legibility refinements" block shows someone already noticed and patched four selectors — then the media query at :2712-2721 re-shrinks .metric-top back to 8px three lines later. A token floor is the only fix that holds.

must_fix_to_reach_8.change: Add bottom: max(22px, env(safe-area-inset-bottom) + 22px) and, inside @media (max-width: 760px), make the toast full-width (left: 12px; right: 12px; max-width: none) so it cannot sit on top of a focused control.

scores.verdict: There is real, competent accessibility engineering here — focus return in dialogs, persistent empty live regions, a skip link, prefers-reduced-motion, an 8.77:1 gold focus ring, mobile 40px/44px targets, fieldset/legend, lang="en", sr-only detail on metric cards. The existing axe pass is not the reason; someone thought about this. But the defects axe cannot see are numerous and several are Level A: four 2.5.3 Label-in-Name failures, meaningful text hidden with aria-hidden, an accessible-name override erasing the pending count, a polling panel wrapped in aria-live, and a type scale reaching 3px.

top_findings.title: Sub-12px type is systemic (130+ declarations, floor 3px) and the provenance layer shrinks most
top_findings.problem: .metric-top .origin-badge { font-size: 5px } at ≤760px; .cover-placeholder 4px at ≤760px and 3px at ≤380px; .agent-state 5px; .eyebrow 8px at 0.17em uppercase; .verification-label and .status-pill 7px. A scan of app/globals.css finds ~130 font-size declarations below 12px against a 13px body. Every one of the product's honesty markers — DEMO, MANUAL SNAPSHOT, NEEDS VERIFICATION, PENDING, WAITING — lands in that band. Contrast is not the problem (I computed every pair: 4.5:1 to 15:1); size is the whole problem. A partial patch exists at :2699 ("Legibility refinements") and is immediately undone by the media query at :2712.
top_findings.proposed_change: Add --text-xs: 11px / --text-sm: 12px tokens at :root (app/globals.css:9-32) and sweep every sub-11px font-size to var(--text-xs), deleting the mobile shrink overrides rather than raising them. Exempt only genuinely decorative cover text (.cover-top/.cover-author/.cover-placeholder), whose container should get aria-hidden instead. No user-visible strings change, so tests/e2e/workspace.spec.ts and experience.spec.ts stay green — but re-run the axe assertions on /, /universe, /desk, /settings since layout shifts.

.desk-preview h2 br { display: none; } hides the
that components/kira/mission-control.tsx:72-75 relies on to separate "A few things" from "need your instinct." JSX strips the whitespace-only lines around the

top_findings.title: The nav suppresses its own descriptions and the pending-decision count from assistive tech
top_findings.problem: The three primary nav Links carry aria-label={title} (lines 121, 139, 161), which overrides all descendant content. The helpful <small> descriptions are additionally aria-hidden="true" (133, 150, 165). The .count-badge at 152-157 tries to compensate with aria-label on a bare <span> — an ARIA-prohibited attribute on role=generic — and is overridden by the parent label regardless. Net effect: a screen-reader user hears "Cassandra's Desk" and never learns there are 3 decisions waiting.
top_findings.proposed_change: Remove the three aria-labels and the three aria-hiddens; change the badge to {count} pending decisions. The link name becomes "Cassandra's Desk Ideas, decisions & your guidance 3 pending decisions".

top_findings.title: The manuscript reading panel is an aria-live region that re-announces on every poll
top_findings.problem: <Card className="library-panel library-progress" aria-live="polite"> wraps an <h2>, a <progress>, the filename, the chunk counters and up to four caveat paragraphs. The component polls while background reading runs, so every increment of completed_chunks re-announces the whole panel. On a novel-length manuscript this makes the page unusable with a screen reader for the entire read — precisely on the surface handling her most intimate material.
top_findings.proposed_change:
Remove aria-live from the Card. Add one dedicated

containing only a throttled sentence ("142 of 310 passages read."), updated at most every ~20 seconds and on state transitions. Add aria-valuetext to the on the same line.

top_findings.title: Four WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name failures (Level A)
top_findings.problem: Accessible names that do not contain the visible label, so voice-control users cannot activate the controls by reading them: workspace-guide.tsx:29 (visible "Guide", name "Open workspace guide"); getting-started.tsx:120 (visible "Hide for now", name "Hide getting started"); app/welcome/page.tsx:22 (visible "KIRA OS AUTHOR INTELLIGENCE", name "KIRA OS sign in"); app/login/page.tsx:27 (same, name "KIRA OS home").
top_findings.proposed_change: Drop the redundant aria-label in all four places and let the visible text name the control. tests/e2e/experience.spec.ts pins button "Open workspace guide" — update that assertion to button "Guide" in the same commit, or change the visible text to "Open guide" and keep the test green.

top_findings.title: Every text input is 12px, so iOS Safari zooms the page on focus
top_findings.problem: [data-slot="input"], [data-slot="textarea"] { font-size: 12px; } overrides the text-base md:text-sm in components/ui/input.tsx:10 and textarea.tsx:9, which exists specifically to keep mobile inputs at 16px. Below 16px iOS auto-zooms on focus. This fires on the login form — her first interaction — and on every field in the desk, studio, learn, plans, connections and access forms.
top_findings.proposed_change: Scope the 12px to @media (min-width: 761px) in app/globals.css:165-169, leaving mobile at 16px; or delete the override entirely and let the component classes apply.

top_findings.title: Native required makes every custom validation message unreachable, and no field is ever marked aria-invalid
top_findings.problem: manual-review-form.tsx:186/:207, studio-page.tsx:85, connected-book-detail.tsx:130, connections-page.tsx and login-form.tsx all use native required. Browser constraint validation blocks submit before the onSubmit handler runs, so the carefully-written messages at manual-review-form.tsx:82 ("Give your idea a title and add the idea you want to review.") and studio-page.tsx:111 ("Write a question of 10 to 6,000 characters.") never appear. Nothing anywhere sets aria-invalid or aria-errormessage, so error paragraphs are never tied to the fields they describe.
top_findings.proposed_change:
Swap required → aria-required={true} on fields whose components implement their own validation, add aria-invalid on failure, and give each error

an id referenced by aria-errormessage. Keep native required only where there is no custom message (login-form.tsx). Also give the character counter at manual-review-form.tsx:197 an id, add it to line 211's aria-describedby, and make it a throttled role="status".

top_findings.title: Every book-card link has a ~25-word accessible name built from decorative placeholder cover text
top_findings.problem: BookCover renders "THE KIRA STANLEY COLLECTION", the title again, "KIRA STANLEY" and "CATALOG PLACEHOLDER · NOT OFFICIAL COVER" inside the <Link className="book-card"> (book-card.tsx:31-47, and again in connected mode at connected-library.tsx:73). Only .cover-ornament is aria-hidden (line 18). A links-list read of /universe returns 8 near-identical 25-word names. The component itself declares the cover a placeholder, so none of that text is informative.
top_findings.proposed_change: Add aria-hidden="true" to the .book-cover div at book-card.tsx:13. Names collapse to "My Alpha Team / 01 Crazy People Book Metadata needs verification". Re-check tests/e2e/workspace.spec.ts, which asserts 8 .book-card elements (unaffected, CSS selector) and link "Crazy People Book" (may now match the book card as well as the search result — disambiguate with a scoped locator).

top_findings.title: Mutually-exclusive filters are built as aria-pressed toggles in 8+ places; three filter groups are unnamed
top_findings.problem: .knowledge-view-nav (3 views), .knowledge-facets (4 facets, line 93), .catalog-filters (universe-catalog.tsx:69, connected-library.tsx:70), .inspiration-filters (inspiration-shelf.tsx:42), .ads-chart-controls / .ads-day-picker / .ads-book-shelf (ads/overview.tsx:36,47,69) and .ads-tabs (ads/dashboard.tsx:35) all use aria-pressed for single-select. AT announces "toggle button, pressed" with no set size or position, so the user cannot tell how many options exist or that selecting one clears the others. Separately, universe-catalog.tsx:69, connected-library.tsx:70 and plans-page.tsx:63 put aria-label on a role=generic <div>, where it is ignored — those three groups have no accessible name at all.
top_findings.proposed_change: Convert single-select sets to role="radiogroup" + role="radio" aria-checked with a roving tabindex, or to Radix Tabs where a panel follows. At minimum add the missing role="group" to the three unnamed divs tonight — that part is a five-minute fix. tests/e2e/workspace.spec.ts asserts filter button "My Alpha Team" by role=button, so a radio conversion in universe-catalog.tsx requires updating that assertion.

top_findings.title: Global toast is a conditionally-mounted live region, shows a success checkmark on errors, and can obscure focus
top_findings.problem: The toast mounts only when state.notice || state.error is truthy, so the live region and its content appear in the same DOM mutation — unreliably announced. Line 403 renders <Check size={16} /> unconditionally, so an error toast displays a checkmark. It never auto-dismisses (confirmed: no setTimeout in lib/db/demo-store.tsx) and is position: fixed; bottom: 22px; right: 22px (app/globals.css:1140), so on a phone it can permanently cover a focused control — WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (AA).
top_findings.proposed_change: Mount two persistent empty regions (role="status" and role="alert") as the app already does correctly at studio-page.tsx:208 and learn-page.tsx:195; make the icon conditional on state.error; and make the toast full-width above the safe-area inset at ≤760px.

top_findings.title: "The minions are working. Go write. 🖤" — tone, product-rule and AT-announcement problem in one string
top_findings.problem: Duplicated at desk-page.tsx:110. "Minions" implies running autonomous agents, which AGENTS.md rule 2 and agent-status.tsx:49 both explicitly deny; the tone is the one place the voice slips from peer to cute; and 🖤 is announced mid-sentence as "black heart".
top_findings.proposed_change: Replace both with "Nothing is waiting on you. Go write." Neither string is pinned — the demo seed always has 3 pending briefs, so this empty state never renders in tests/e2e/workspace.spec.ts or experience.spec.ts.
top_findings.owner_decision_needed: Whether the in-group warmth vocabulary ("the coven" at mission-control.tsx:143, "the minions") is Michael-and-Cassy shorthand she will enjoy or filler that should go. I would cut "minions" regardless because it contradicts the no-running-agents rule; "the coven" is a taste call only the owner can make.

top_findings.title: #setup quick link scrolls without moving focus, unlike its sibling anchor
top_findings.problem: settings-page.tsx:58-59 offers two in-page anchors. #account-password works because password-settings.tsx:50 has role="region" tabIndex={-1}. #setup (setup-status.tsx:50) has neither, so activating "Your connections" scrolls the viewport but leaves focus on the link — the keyboard user's next Tab goes to the third quick link, not into the section they just requested.
top_findings.proposed_change: Add role="region" tabIndex={-1} to <Card id="setup"> at setup-status.tsx:50, matching the existing pattern one file over.

what_works: Focus management in dialogs is better than most shipped React apps. app-shell.tsx:417-418 sends focus to "Keep working" on open and back to the sign-out button on close; approval-card.tsx:167-175 focuses Cancel for approve/reject and, when the card unmounts because the brief moved to the Reviewed tab, falls back to #desk-reviewed-tab; book-detail.tsx:215 returns to the Prepare button. Do not regress this.

The persistent-empty live-region pattern is used correctly in five places: studio-page.tsx:208, learn-page.tsx:195, manual-review-form.tsx:238, book-knowledge.tsx:90 (a role="status" index caption that updates as she searches) and connections-page.tsx:109. Keep this and make the global toast match it, not the reverse.

Focus-to-error with tabIndex={-1} + ref.focus() is implemented consistently — login-form.tsx:30/52, manual-review-form.tsx:83/220, learn-page.tsx:194, connections-page.tsx:106, one-time-sign-in.tsx:112, access-page.tsx:95/119.

components/kira/getting-started.tsx is a model dismissible-panel implementation: aria-labelledby, focus to the reopen button on hide (line 65), focus to the heading on show (line 70), icons aria-hidden, and an sr-only "Complete: " prefix at line 131.

The colour system genuinely passes. I computed every token pair from app/globals.css: #85887b/#121312 = 5.15:1, #a6a79c = 7.65:1, #959982 = 6.35:1, #949782 = 6.22:1 — all above 4.5:1 on all three surface colours; the gold focus ring #c7af83 is 8.77:1; white on --destructive #b35460 is 4.82:1. Nothing needs recolouring, only resizing.

Mobile touch targets are already handled at app/globals.css:2740-2747 (button, a[data-slot="button"] { min-height: 40px }, .nav-item { min-height: 44px }) — above the 24px SC 2.5.8 AA floor and close to the 44px AAA target. Preserve this when refactoring the type scale.

prefers-reduced-motion is handled globally and correctly at app/globals.css:2689-2697, including neutralising html { scroll-behavior: smooth } (line 64) via the * selector. desk-page.tsx:27 additionally uses behavior: "instant" for its programmatic scroll.

Native semantics are used where they belong: <details>/<summary> for every disclosure (context-help.tsx:49, approval-card.tsx:83, learn-page.tsx nested lessons, daily-quote.tsx:16), <fieldset>/<legend> for grouped inputs (learn-page.tsx:61, studio-page.tsx:83, plans-page.tsx), <dl> in book-detail.tsx:91, <figure>/<figcaption>/<blockquote>/<cite> in daily-quote.tsx, and a real <progress> element rather than a div.

components/kira/login-form.tsx is the best-built form in the app: real label associations, correct autoComplete tokens, aria-describedby on the password field conditional on the error, role=alert, focus to the error, and the password cleared on failure (line 29).

External links consistently carry (opens in a new tab) (connections-page.tsx:96, :137), and daily-quote.tsx:12 builds the warning into an aria-label that still contains the visible text — 2.5.3-compliant, unlike the four cases flagged above.

lucide-react v1.47's hasA11yProp adds aria-hidden automatically when no a11y prop is passed (node_modules/lucide-react/dist/esm/Icon.mjs:42), so the hundreds of bare <Icon size={n} /> calls are already safe. Do not bulk-add redundant aria-hidden; it is noise.

The skip link (app-shell.tsx:324 + app/globals.css:1909-1921), <main tabIndex={-1}> (app-shell.tsx:382), <html lang="en"> (app/layout.tsx:91), the <nav aria-label="Main navigation"> landmark, and the correct aria-expanded/aria-controls/hidden disclosure on "Coming later" (app-shell.tsx:170-183) are all in place.

metric-card.tsx:42 supplies {metric.detail}. Demo data., so provenance that is visually 5px is at least correct for screen readers; and inspiration-shelf.tsx:49-61 implements a real APG carousel — sr-only key instructions, aria-roledescription="carousel", arrow/Home/End handling that defers to nested controls, and a scoped aria-live position readout that includes the idea title.
